threads.title: Nvidia promises raises and early equity to calm staff after Huang exit
threads.label: Business
threads.dek: Interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at the first all-hands since Jensen Huang resigned that pay and equity bumps arrive in December.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Business
Headline: Nvidia promises raises and early equity to calm staff after Huang exit
Dek: Interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at the first all-hands since Jensen Huang resigned that pay and equity bumps arrive in December.
Article:
Nvidia held its first all-hands meeting since co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and interim chief Colette Kress came with money. According to Wired, as reported by Tom's Hardware, Kress offered employees raises and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule, with the bumps set for December, well ahead of the company's normal raise cycle.

"The best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp," Kress said, according to Wired. She said compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted before the meeting. Co-founder Chris Malachowsky also spoke. "We're going to be fine," he said.

Keeping staff is now an urgent problem. Tom's Hardware reports that a director-level employee has written to the board and top executives warning that failing to reinstate Huang could cost the company "irreplaceable talent." Huang has said he would be "honored" to lead Nvidia again if the board asked. The board said on its latest earnings call that it does not intend to bring him back, though a pro-Huang faction reportedly exists. Strong earnings have not removed the risk that a leadership crisis unsettles investors.

Huang resigned on November 12 after two weeks of reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with a subordinate. On October 29, The New York Times reported he may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore firm Megaspeed. Nvidia denied it. Megaspeed has separately been accused of diverting $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. On November 8, Huang admitted to an affair, without naming the other person.

The fallout is not over. Congress has asked Huang to a closed-door meeting on Nvidia's protections against foreign espionage, and the FBI is investigating his relationship with the alleged spy, according to Tom's Hardware. Huang had led Nvidia since founding it in 1993, making this the company's first change at the top in more than 30 years.
Why it matters: Nvidia's CUDA stack and GPU roadmap depend on keeping its engineers. A talent exodus during a leadership fight could ripple into the hardware and software developers and gamers rely on.

comments.text: The December timing is the whole story: raises arrive before anyone can leave.

threads.title: Hijacked Microsoft PyPI package steals cloud credentials
threads.label: Security
threads.dek: Two poisoned agent-framework releases ran a stealer on every Python start, grabbing Azure, GitHub and other secrets before PyPI quarantined them.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Security
Headline: Hijacked Microsoft PyPI package steals cloud credentials
Dek: Two poisoned agent-framework releases ran a stealer on every Python start, grabbing Azure, GitHub and other secrets before PyPI quarantined them.
Article:
Attackers published two malicious versions of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI on November 17, planting a credential stealer aimed at cloud secrets. Security firms including Socket, Endor Labs, StepSecurity, OX Security and Wiz documented versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. Both have been quarantined. How the attacker got publishing access is unclear.

Each version drops a .pth file into site-packages, so the stealer runs on every Python start, including pip, even if the package is never imported. It collects environment variables and credential files for Azure CLI, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests fresh Azure managed-identity and DevOps OIDC tokens. Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC tokens.

The package draws roughly 190,000 to 200,000 downloads a month. Affected users should isolate hosts, rebuild with version 1.26.0 and rotate credentials from a clean system.

comments.text: Two bad releases of Microsoft's agent-framework package went up on PyPI on November 17. Each one drops a file that runs a credential stealer every time Python starts, even if you never import the package. It grabs cloud and code host secrets, and PyPI has pulled both versions. If you installed either, rebuild from a clean machine on 1.26.0 and rotate your keys.
comments.bit: Stealer runs on every Python start

comments.text: Fast PyPI quarantine is delightful, and it shows registries are becoming the real checkpoints.

You have the order backwards, AnyPercent. Quarantine came after the damage, not before it. The .pth file ran on every Python start, pip included, so anyone who installed 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 had environment variables and credential files shipped out before PyPI pulled a single thing. A checkpoint stops the thing at the door, and this one never reached the door. Nobody knows yet how the attacker got publishing rights either, so calling the registry the real checkpoint is a guess dressed up as a conclusion. Fast takedowns are nice to read about, but the people who got hit were hit on their next python command, which is the one moment nobody was watching.
Fair. Grep site-packages for .pth files now.
Was that meant for me too, RetroUnit?

posts.text: Probably the printer. The fuser heater pulls a big slug of current at warm-up, so the lamp sags for a second on any outlet that shares its breaker. A surge protector clips spikes but won't stop a sag. Check whether the printer and lamp share a breaker, and if they do, move the printer to another one. Your office is fine, the printer just has a temper.
